MIXED ROTATIONCyclicals +0.2% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The tape is all-in on risk, and the most stretched trade isn't a sector, it's the death of utilities. XLE/XLU sits at a z-score of 2.19, in the top 0% of its yearly range, meaning every prior reading is lower than today's. XLK is up 11.48% this month and 28.68% year-to-date while XLU is down 4.85% in the same month and -1.04% on the year. That's not a slow bleed, it's an exodus. The same story shows up in XLF/XLU at 2.10, top 0%, and SPY/IEF at 1.93, top 3%. You're watching a market that has decided defense is dead money.

Themes confirm it. Gold miners are up 34.4% in a month, uranium 20.1%, software 18.8%, AI infra 18.7%, and quantum 17.3%. That's a liquidity flood into the most speculative pockets. Energy is up 9.5% this month and 46.1% year-to-date. You'd expect that kind of risk appetite to be fragile, but the breadth is genuine: 11 of 16 theme baskets are positive this month. Even biotech at 3.7% and defense at 6.1% are hanging on. The only negative theme is GLP-1 at -1.7%, and that's a single-name story, not a risk signal.

The ratios tell you where the pain is concentrated. GDX/GLD at 2.61 in the top 1% of its yearly range says miners are running far ahead of the metal itself, which means levered speculation on gold, not a safe-haven trade. HYG/LQD at 2.28 and HYG/IEF at 2.12 both sit in the top 0% to 4%, meaning credit risk is being rewarded with no fear premium. Meanwhile XLU/SPY is at -2.16, bottom 0%, and TLT/SPY is at -1.83, bottom 5%. The second-order read: positioning is so crowded in cyclicals and so abandoned in defensives that any whiff of growth concern, any rates hiccup, triggers a violent reversal in these ratios. You want to be nimble, not loyal. The tell to flip this whole read is XLU/SPY turning positive for two consecutive weeks, which has not happened once in this dataset.

Cyclicals and risk assets lead, defensives and long duration are abandoned, but the stretch itself is the vulnerability.

BULL

The breadth is real: 11 of 16 theme baskets are positive this month and XLK, XLE, and XLY are all up +5% or more. Credit ratios at top-of-range z-scores confirm liquidity is chasing risk, and gold miners outperforming gold itself means speculative flows, not just hedging.

BEAR

XLU/SPY at bottom 0% of its yearly range and TLT/SPY at bottom 5% show absolute abandonment of defensives. When no one owns the hedge, any exogenous shock lands on a market with zero cushion, and the most crowded trades, semis, AI infra, gold miners, become the biggest source of forced selling.

TELL

The specific move that resolves it is XLU/SPY breaking back above its prior month's high, which would signal rotation into defensives and a unwind of every stretched cyclical ratio.

⚠ Sector breadth shows cyclicals broadly leading: **XLK**, **XLE**, **XLY**, **XLC**, **XLV**, **XLB**, and **XLF** all positive this month, with **XLE** up **37.31%** year-to-date. vs The standout laggard is **XLI** at only **0.27%** for the month and **12.13%** year-to-date, plus **XLU** deeply negative at **-4.85%** monthly, suggesting the market is rewarding sectors with high beta but not all cyclicals equally.: The conflict is between a broad cyclical bid in most sectors and the selective nature of that bid once you look inside: industrials are flat while energy and tech run double digits. You trust the thematic data over the sector-level breadth because the theme baskets show where the actual flows are going, into AI infra, semis, and energy, while industrials and utilities are being used as funding sources.

The extreme readings worth watching for mean reversion are the ones where a ratio has run so far that it's pricing in a regime that never lasts. GDX/GLD at z 2.61 and in the top 1% of its yearly range is the most stretched: miners up 34.4% in a month against a metal that itself has been strong.

That kind of divergence usually gives back fast. HYG/IEF at 2.12 and in the top 0% of its yearly range is another candidate, credit returning to no-risk pricing while government bond exposure is at bottom 0%.

The reversion candidates are the ones tied to sentiment extremes, not fundamentals. The confirmed trends are the cyclical versus defensive spreads: XLE/XLU at 2.19 and top 0%, XLF/XLU at 2.10 and top 0%.

Those have been one-way for the entire sample and they show no sign of rolling over within the data. Same with SPY/TLT at 1.94 and top 4%.

You treat those as trends until the tell breaks, not as automatic fade candidates.
